finding: Ray-star lemma (proved here, uses TMFI plus adopted GAP3). Let C be an intrinsic component of dimension r>=2 of a member Q of a four-MOQLS(8), S its real projector span (dimension b). For an actual ray u of C let sigma_u = dim span{P_v : v ray of C orthogonal to u} and L_u the real subspace of u-perp such that P_u Z P_{u-perp}, Z in S, equals u chi* with chi in L_u. Then dim_R L_u <= b-1-sigma_u (S meets the u/u-perp block-diagonal algebra in at least P_u plus the star span). Phase-normalizing <v,u> > 0, every u-active ray v (0<|<u,v>|<1) has P_{u-perp} v in L_u. (i) If L_u lies in a complex line Cw, all u-active rays lie in span(u,w); for a mixed one v, rays orthogonal to v are its in-plane partner or lie in u-perp intersect w-perp (dimension r-2), so the partner is forced in every line through v; TMFI at a=u gives at least three partner cells off v's row and column, and with the forced partner in v's row and column the partner multiplicity is >=5, contradicting GAP3. (ii) If dim L_u = 2 and Im<.,.> is not identically zero on L_u, any two orthogonal u-active rays have A-parts that are real multiples of each other, so again only the in-plane partner is u-active and orthogonal, the same closedness holds, and TMFI plus GAP3 give a contradiction. Hence for every actual ray u: dim_R L_u >= 2, and if = 2 then L_u is Lagrangian (all u-active rays, phase-normalized, lie in the real Euclidean 3-space R u + L_u). Consequently sigma_u <= b-3 for every ray.
application_state_C4_span8: For an intrinsic C4 with b=8 this gives sigma_u <= 5 for every ray: the star of each ray (all rays orthogonal to it) is a 3-dimensional configuration of projector span at most 5 (minimal irreducible span or reducible).
